rfm_tuples.R: We have in the past identified material weaknesses in our internal control over financial reporting... our prior material weakness related to our income tax provision resulted in the restatement of our unaudited condensed consolidated financial statements for the quarters and year-to-date periods ended March 31, 2022, June 30, 2022, and September 30, 2022. Management concluded that our internal control over financial reporting was effective as of December 31, 2023.
rfm_tuples.f: Verify remediation was independently audited (PwC) and that no new material weaknesses surfaced in subsequent 10-Q; cross-check critical audit matter disclosure.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Item 9A + PwC audit opinion; Q1 2024 10-Q Item 4 Controls and Procedures
rfm_tuples.M_value: PwC opinion 2024-02-29 confirms remediation. However, PwC explicitly carries forward revenue recognition as a Critical Audit Matter precisely because 'material weaknesses existed during the year related to this matter.' Q1 2024 10-Q discloses ongoing implementation of new revenue recognition accounting software 'which we expect to complete in the first quarter of 2024' — i.e., the system change underpinning remediation was still being finalized at the time of the 10-K.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Remediation was certified but is fragile: the underlying revenue-recognition software cutover was concurrent with the remediation conclusion. PwC retains revenue recognition as a CAM. Honest disclosure of a real residual risk — not concealment, but a Mode B vulnerability.

rfm_tuples.R: At December 31, 2023 and March 31, 2024, we had no amounts outstanding under our 2021 Revolving Facility or any outstanding letters of credit and we were in compliance with all financial covenants. The 2021 Revolving Facility requires compliance with a total net first lien leverage ratio of 4.50 to 1.00... The Financial Covenant will be tested at quarter-end only if the total principal amount... exceeds 35%.
rfm_tuples.f: Verify zero-draw status and cash position via balance sheet; cross-check covenant geometry; check if covenant is even active.
rfm_tuples.M_source: Q1 2024 10-Q balance sheet; Note 5 Long-term Debt
rfm_tuples.M_value: Cash and cash equivalents $228.1M at 3/31/2024 (vs $225.7M at 12/31/2023, GROWING). Zero revolver draw means the 4.5x leverage covenant is not even tested (springs only above 35% utilization). Free cash flow Q1 2024 $24.7M vs Q1 2023 $21.8M (+13%). Net income Q1 2024 +$4.7M vs Q1 2023 net loss ($2.4M).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Balance sheet is genuinely clean: net cash of ~$228M with zero debt drawn, growing FCF, and a covenant that is structurally dormant. This is the opposite of distressed-small-cap profile despite the -38.8% drawdown.

rfm_tuples.R: Our business primarily depends on business formations. The number of business formations on our platform is subject to unpredictable declines or fluctuations... In the three months ended March 31, 2024, we experienced an 18% decrease in business formation transactions... Our business formations lagged behind the 2% decrease in overall U.S. business formations.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B — derive: if the headwind is admitted, what should be quantitatively verifiable in the KPI ladder? Compare formation counts across 10-Qs.
rfm_tuples.M_value: The sequential narrative shows a sharp inflection: FY23 +23% YoY, Q3 2023 +17% YoY, then Q1 2024 -18% YoY. LZ's formation losses (-18%) materially outpaced the broader market decline (-2% per LZ's own US Census reference), implying ~16pp share loss, not just macro. Average order value also fell because of free LLC strategy. Transaction revenue: $66.3M Q1'24 vs $68.0M Q1'23 (-2.5%) — modest, but is masked by subscription growth.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B finding. Company correctly states the YoY decline but understates that they LOST SHARE vs the US market — they only mention the absolute decline. This is the strongest distress signal in LZ's filing: the freemium-LLC strategy launched Q1 2023 appears to be cannibalizing transaction revenue and ceding share, not just a macro headwind.

rfm_tuples.R: On March 7, 2024, Dan Wernikoff, our Chief Executive Officer, entered into a trading plan intended to satisfy the affirmative defense of Rule 10b5-1(c) under the Exchange Act. The 10b5-1 plan... will be in effect until the earlier of (1) March 7, 2025, and (2) the date on which 1,000,000 shares of the Company's common stock have been sold under such 10b5-1 plan.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B — cross-reference CEO 10b5-1 sales plan against (a) ongoing $100M buyback program and (b) -38.8% drawdown context.
rfm_tuples.M_source: Q1 2024 10-Q Item 5; October 2023 board buyback authorization; share repurchase table
rfm_tuples.M_value: Company repurchased 1.2M shares at avg $10.91 in Q1 2024 ($12.8M), with $87.2M remaining authorization. Simultaneously, CEO adopts plan to SELL up to 1.0M shares over 12 months. The asymmetry: company communicates 'buy our stock' via buyback while CEO is preparing to sell up to ~$10M-$11M of stock at depressed prices.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B insider-behavior signal. Wernikoff's 10b5-1 plan does not itself indicate misconduct (legal, disclosed), but the cohabitation with corporate buyback during drawdown is a soft negative. Plan was adopted at depressed prices (~$10-11) suggesting either liquidity need or low conviction in near-term recovery.

rfm_tuples.R: On February 15, 2024, it was determined that Rich Preece, Chief Operating Officer, would transition from LegalZoom effective as of March 31, 2024. Subject to Mr. Preece's entrance into a separation agreement... Mr. Preece will be entitled to receive the severance benefits payable under Section 4(a)(i) of the Employment Agreement.
rfm_tuples.f: Verify whether COO departure was previously signaled and whether replacement disclosed; check 8-K disclosure mechanism.
rfm_tuples.M_value: COO departure was disclosed jointly with Q4 earnings (Item 2.02 + Item 5.02 in same 8-K), which is a buried-bad-news disclosure pattern. No successor named in 10-K or Q1 10-Q. Combined with November 2023 director Dipan Patel resignation following Permira's full exit, this is the second senior-team change in 4 months.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Co-disclosed with earnings is mild stagecraft (legal but optimized for low signal). No successor is a real Mode B gap — the COO role overseeing the freemium-to-subscription conversion strategy is unfilled during the inflection period when business formations are declining 18%. Material vacancy.

rfm_tuples.R: On November 13, 2023, following the closing of the Secondary Offering, Dipan Patel, a Class I director who was initially nominated by Permira, resigned as a member of the Board of Directors, effective immediately... Upon the closing of the Secondary Offering, Permira ceased to own any shares of Common Stock and, accordingly, Permira lost its right to nominate a director.
rfm_tuples.f: Verify Permira's exit pricing and timing; reconcile with company buyback footprint.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Permira sold 14M shares at $10.00 in September 2023 (with concurrent company buyback of 4.7M shares at $9.55 from Permira) and 15.1M shares in November 2023. Sponsor was fully out by November 2023. LZ stock then declined from ~$12 (Sept 2023) to ~$8.43 (May 15, 2024) per drawdown context.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Permira's complete exit at $10 (with company facilitating via $45M direct repurchase) preceded the steep formation decline reported in Q1 2024. This is sponsor information asymmetry: PE sponsor with board seat and full diligence access fully exited 5-6 months before the public KPI deterioration became visible. Honestly disclosed in real time but a strong adverse signal.

rfm_tuples.R: We have served as the Company's auditor since 2006. /s/ PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP
rfm_tuples.f: Verify auditor tenure, Big-4 status, and any historical disagreements.
rfm_tuples.M_source: PCAOB ID 238 (PwC LLP, Big 4); 10-K Item 9 (no auditor changes or disagreements disclosed); restatement history in Item 9A relates to internal control, not auditor disagreement
rfm_tuples.M_value: PwC since 2006 (~18 years), Big 4, retained through 2022 restatement and material weakness identification. No reportable disagreements. CAM disclosed on revenue recognition is standard given the recent material weakness.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Auditor quality is genuinely high. Tenure of 18 years could be a soft watch-item for independence but is not a red flag at a Big 4.

rfm_tuples.R: Due to a large and diverse customer base, no individual customer represented more than 10% of our consolidated revenue for the three months ended March 31, 2024 and 2023... presented less than 1% of our unaudited consolidated revenue for the three months ended March 31, 2024 and 2023 [foreign].
rfm_tuples.f: Verify customer concentration claim; cross-check with subscription unit count.
rfm_tuples.M_source: Q1 2024 10-Q Concentrations of Credit; 10-K customer footnote; subscription units 1.605M at 3/31/2024
rfm_tuples.M_value: 1.605M subscription units (vs 1.501M Q1 2023, +7%) with ARPU $272 — implies highly granular base. Claim is internally consistent.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Customer concentration is genuinely diversified across SMB base. No mirror disclosure needed (no enterprise anchor).

rfm_tuples.R: We are continuing to scale up LZ Tax and we are learning more about our tax customers in the process. As we optimize our LZ Tax offerings to better meet the needs of our target customers, we are seeing and expect to continue to see a decrease in the number of customers purchasing and retaining an LZ Tax subscription unit. While this decrease will produce a revenue headwind throughout 2024, we expect increased retention of our LZ Tax subscription units over the long term.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B — derive what isn't said: is there a specific magnitude, a churn rate, a cohort retention curve, or unit count for LZ Tax disclosed?
rfm_tuples.M_source: Q1 2024 10-Q narrative; Q3 2023 10-Q identical 'into 2024' language; no separate LZ Tax KPI table
rfm_tuples.M_value: Same softening narrative appears in Q3 2023 ('into 2024') and Q1 2024 ('throughout 2024'), suggesting the headwind is widening, not narrowing. LZ does not disclose LZ Tax subscription unit count, ARPU, or attach rate as a separate line — only aggregate subscription units (which grew 7%). The aggregate masks LZ Tax-specific shrinkage.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B disclosure gap. LegalZoom acquired LZ Tax from Inc Authority (2022) and Earth Class Mail tail, marketing it as core to the freemium-conversion thesis. By omitting LZ Tax-specific KPIs while admitting both an aggregate headwind and 'optimization,' management makes it impossible to verify whether the tax bet is succeeding. Honesty-alpha framework: this is verifiable obscurity, not lying, but it should be priced.

rfm_tuples.R: During the quarter ended September 30, 2022, following an evaluation of our office space and business requirements, we commenced a plan to sell our operational headquarters in Austin, Texas... The estimated fair value less costs to sell the assets held for sale exceed their carrying values and hence no impairment was necessary during the quarter ended March 31, 2024. Total assets held for sale $22,722 [thousand].
rfm_tuples.f: Verify timing: in October 2023 8-K, LZ announced sale of the 9900 Spectrum Drive Austin property to Trinity Foundation RE Venture for $41M, with 6-month leaseback. Reconcile against the $22.7M carrying value still on the Q1 2024 balance sheet.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Asset was contracted to sell for $41M in October 2023 with Buyer due-diligence deadline November 22, 2023; closing expected shortly thereafter. By Q1 2024 (March 31, 2024), $22.7M remains classified as held for sale — meaning the Trinity deal apparently did NOT close, or closed but a different building portion remains. The 10-Q discloses only that 'fair value less costs to sell exceed carrying values' but does not narrate the deal status.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B — claim evolution gap. The October 2023 8-K announced a specific $41M sale with a specific counterparty and timeline. Six months later, the asset is still on the balance sheet at $22.7M with no narrative explaining whether Trinity closed, walked, or partial-closed. Either the deal fell through (negative signal that should have been an 8-K) or only one building sold (under-disclosure of progress). Indicates buyer due-diligence break or renegotiation.

supplemental_signals.balance_sheet_strength: Cash $228.1M, zero debt drawn, generates +$24.7M FCF/qtr. Drawdown is multiple-compression, not distress.
leadership_changes: COO Rich Preece departure 3/31/2024 (co-disclosed with earnings)
CEO Wernikoff 10b5-1 sell plan adopted 3/7/2024 (up to 1.0M shares)
supplemental_signals.sponsor_exit: Permira fully exited Sept-Nov 2023 via two secondaries ($10.00 and undisclosed November price) with LZ buying $45M directly at $9.55
supplemental_signals.kpi_inflection: Business formations: +23% FY23 -> -18% Q1 2024 vs market -2%, implying material share loss
supplemental_signals.cam_residual_risk: Revenue recognition Critical Audit Matter retained due to recent material weakness; new accounting software implementation completing Q1 2024
supplemental_signals.buyback_pace: 1.2M shares at avg $10.91 in Q1 2024; $87.2M of $100M authorization remaining

summary: LZ is NOT a distressed/lying small cap. Balance sheet is clean (net cash $228M, zero debt, growing FCF, no covenant exposure), auditor is Big-4 with remediated controls, and disclosures are largely honest. The drawdown reflects a real KPI inflection: business formations down 18% YoY in Q1 2024 vs -2% for the US market = ~16pp share loss tied to the company's own freemium-LLC pivot. Mode B findings are the strongest: (1) Permira's full PE-sponsor exit at $10 in late 2023 just ahead of the KPI deterioration, (2) CEO 10b5-1 sell plan adopted during the drawdown alongside corporate buybacks, (3) Austin HQ sale appears to have stalled vs the October 2023 $41M agreement, (4) LZ Tax disclosed as a 'headwind' without any LZ-Tax-specific KPI to verify. Verdict: NEUTRAL with mild negative tilt — honesty-alpha framework does not flag lying, but the freemium strategy is destroying transaction economics faster than subscription growth offsets it.
